subject: Huge density peaks from SPDE model

messages.author: 928a129fe0016f39
messages.subject: Huge density peaks from SPDE model
parts:
Hi,

I have a spatio-temporal model similar to Cameletti et al. 2012 and it seems to give reasonable parameter estimates. However, interpolating over the mesh I see the density explode near the borders (see the attachment). Width of the offset area is about same size as the study area and twice as the estimated range. I also extended the offset area width ten times and estimated the model but again a huge spike appeared just outside the study area. Why this happens and what can I do to fix it? Is my mesh somehow improper? I am expecting to get density approaching average outside the study area or so. Otherwise the model seems fine, but this messes up visualizing the results.

Thanks

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Huge density peaks from SPDE model
parts:
Hi,

It looks like you've plotted the results as a piecewise constant function? If not, there is still something strange about the plot itself.

Extrapolation effects can occur if there is a consistent gradient at the edge of the data, but I wouldn't expect it to look quite like this. First, double check that you are indeed looking at the posterior mean and not the posterior standard deviation. Second, also check whether the posterior median behaves like this. Is your observation likelihood Gaussian, or is there a nonlinear link function involved?

Finn

> exp(summary.linear.predictor), but which they only partially do?

almost, use linear.predictor instead. you have to do a change of
variable since linear.predictor is random and if its variability is
large then the mean can blow up. the quantiles are easier and found by
exp() the quantiles, so this is why you'll find the median much more
'stable'.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Huge density peaks from SPDE model
parts:
The transformed posterior medians of linear.predictor should match the posterior medians of fitted.values, yes. Also the other quantiles. The mean depends on the variance as well, since the log-link makes that much more volatile.

It's hard to tell from those summaries what's going on, and your original plot doesn't really show local large peaks; it shows some systematic effect towards the boundary, as well as some very strange discontinuities.  Can you please provide summary(inlaresult) and summary(mesh) and the code you use for plotting? (The rest of the code might also be useful for seeing if there is a bug in that.)
The std.dev. should be increasing outside the region where you have data, and also closer to the boundary, so it's really only the data rich domain that's relevant.

Finn

parts:
Here is a density plot attached for exp(linear.predictor[predicted_stack_index,]$mean) for one of the years which covers only the observation area. The strange thing here is that the density appears to be higher in the north than in the south on average. However, this cannot be the case since the observations get smaller values in the north on average. One of the fixed effects in the model is the vertical coordinate which increases from south to north and it gets estimated as negative as expected, i.e. there is a negative density gradient from south to north. Also, many of the density values at the mesh nodes are much larger than the nearby observed values (the observed values match closely to exp(linear.predictor[observed_stack_index,]$mean)). These patterns repeat over the other years.

See the summary(inlaresult) and summary(mesh) below. One of the things that stands out is the very high value for GroupRho, but I'm not sure if I should worry about it. I'm using INLA through a package, so the code is not readily available. I can try to isolate the INLA part if this doesn't get clearer.

parts:
Here is the code:

# Scale coordinates
coord.scale <- 1e-6
data$xs <- data$x * coord.scale
data$ys <- data$y * coord.scale
coord <- cbind(data$xs, data$ys)

# Create mesh
boundary1 <- inla.nonconvex.hull(points = coord, convex = 0.05)
boundary2 <- inla.nonconvex.hull(points = coord, convex = 0.50)
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = coord, boundary = list(boundary1, boundary2), cutoff = 2e4 * coord.scale,
                     max.edge = c(5e4, 6e5) * coord.scale, offset  = c(1e4, 1e6) * coord.scale)

# Set spatial prior
mesh.width <- min(diff(range(mesh$loc[,1])), diff(range(mesh$loc[,2])))
spde <- local.inla.spde2.matern.new(mesh = mesh, prior.pc.rho = c(mesh.width / 2, 0.5), prior.pc.sig = c(1, 0.5))

# Get temporal and spatial indexes
year <- data$year
year.index <- year - min(year) + 1
n.year <- length(unique(year.index))
spatial.index <- inla.spde.make.index("spatial", n.spde = spde$n.spde, n.group = n.year)

# Create observation stack
A.obs <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = coord, group = year.index, n.group = n.year)
covariates.obs <- c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x6", "x7", "x8")
effects.obs <- list(c(spatial.index, list(intercept = 1)), list(data[, covariates.obs]))
stack.obs <- inla.stack(data = list(count = data$count, E = data$effort), A = list(A.obs, 1), effects = effects.obs, tag = "obs")

# Create prediction stack
coord.mesh <- cbind(rep(mesh$loc[,1], n.year), rep(mesh$loc[,2], n.year))
A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = coord.mesh, group = rep(1:n.year, each = mesh$n), n.group = n.year)
effects.pred <- list(c(spatial.index, list(intercept = 1)))
stack.pred <- inla.stack(data = list(count = NA, E = 1), A = list(A.pred), effects = effects.pred, tag = "pred")

# Combine stacks
stack.all <- inla.stack(stack.obs, stack.pred)
data.stack <- inla.stack.data(stack = stack.all, spde = spde)

# Specify model formula
formula <- count ~ -1 + intercept + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x6 + x7 + x8 +
  f(spatial, model = spde, group = spatial.group, control.group = list(model = "ar1"))

# Estimate model
result <- inla(formula, data = data.stack, family = "nbinomial", E = data$E,
               control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack.all), link = 1, compute = TRUE),
               control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, mlik = TRUE),
               verbose = TRUE)

On Tuesday, 6 December 2016 01:05:13 UTC+7, Finn Lindgren wrote:
Hi,

It looks like you've plotted the results as a piecewise constant function? If not, there is still something strange about the plot itself.

Extrapolation effects can occur if there is a consistent gradient at the edge of the data, but I wouldn't expect it to look quite like this. First, double check that you are indeed looking at the posterior mean and not the posterior standard deviation. Second, also check whether the posterior median behaves like this. Is your observation likelihood Gaussian, or is there a nonlinear link function involved?

Finn

The correlation I got by taking mean over each year for observations and estimates and the correlating the mean densities over the years.

On Sunday, 25 December 2016 14:51:25 UTC+7, Jussi wrote:
Here is the code:

# Scale coordinates
coord.scale <- 1e-6
data$xs <- data$x * coord.scale
data$ys <- data$y * coord.scale
coord <- cbind(data$xs, data$ys)

# Create mesh
boundary1 <- inla.nonconvex.hull(points = coord, convex = 0.05)
boundary2 <- inla.nonconvex.hull(points = coord, convex = 0.50)
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = coord, boundary = list(boundary1, boundary2), cutoff = 2e4 * coord.scale,
                     max.edge = c(5e4, 6e5) * coord.scale, offset  = c(1e4, 1e6) * coord.scale)

# Set spatial prior
mesh.width <- min(diff(range(mesh$loc[,1])), diff(range(mesh$loc[,2])))
spde <- local.inla.spde2.matern.new(mesh = mesh, prior.pc.rho = c(mesh.width / 2, 0.5), prior.pc.sig = c(1, 0.5))

# Get temporal and spatial indexes
year <- data$year
year.index <- year - min(year) + 1
n.year <- length(unique(year.index))
spatial.index <- inla.spde.make.index("spatial", n.spde = spde$n.spde, n.group = n.year)

# Create observation stack
A.obs <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = coord, group = year.index, n.group = n.year)
covariates.obs <- c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x6", "x7", "x8")
effects.obs <- list(c(spatial.index, list(intercept = 1)), list(data[, covariates.obs]))
stack.obs <- inla.stack(data = list(count = data$count, E = data$effort), A = list(A.obs, 1), effects = effects.obs, tag = "obs")

# Create prediction stack
coord.mesh <- cbind(rep(mesh$loc[,1], n.year), rep(mesh$loc[,2], n.year))
A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = coord.mesh, group = rep(1:n.year, each = mesh$n), n.group = n.year)
effects.pred <- list(c(spatial.index, list(intercept = 1)))
stack.pred <- inla.stack(data = list(count = NA, E = 1), A = list(A.pred), effects = effects.pred, tag = "pred")

# Combine stacks
stack.all <- inla.stack(stack.obs, stack.pred)
data.stack <- inla.stack.data(stack = stack.all, spde = spde)

# Specify model formula
formula <- count ~ -1 + intercept + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x6 + x7 + x8 +
  f(spatial, model = spde, group = spatial.group, control.group = list(model = "ar1"))

# Estimate model
result <- inla(formula, data = data.stack, family = "nbinomial", E = data$E,
               control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack.all), link = 1, compute = TRUE),
               control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, mlik = TRUE),
               verbose = TRUE)




On Saturday, 10 December 2016 15:05:39 UTC+7, Finn Lindgren wrote:
The transformed posterior medians of linear.predictor should match the posterior medians of fitted.values, yes. Also the other quantiles. The mean depends on the variance as well, since the log-link makes that much more volatile.

It's hard to tell from those summaries what's going on, and your original plot doesn't really show local large peaks; it shows some systematic effect towards the boundary, as well as some very strange discontinuities.  Can you please provide summary(inlaresult) and summary(mesh) and the code you use for plotting? (The rest of the code might also be useful for seeing if there is a bug in that.)
The std.dev. should be increasing outside the region where you have data, and also closer to the boundary, so it's really only the data rich domain that's relevant.

Finn
